race.name: King Ridge Grasshopper
race.tagline: A 91-mile Sonoma road stage scored across three savage climbing segments.

vitals.field_size: Several hundred riders; exact 2026 count not published
vitals.start_format: Open-road ride with three chip-timed climbing segments for the long course
vitals.registration: 2026 registration closed; no official 2027 edition published
vitals.entry_fee: Not preserved on the completed 2026 event page
vitals.cutoff_time: Timed-segment closing windows; no overall finish cutoff published

climate.description: Cool coastal mornings, possible fog, changing ridge exposure, and afternoon wind.

terrain.surface: 96% paved and 4% dirt; the organizer recommends a road bike with 30-32 mm slick tires

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Scored 2026-08-06 from the organizer's 2026 route and independent race coverage. Kept in Roadie Labs because the official course is 96% paved and the organizer calls it a road stage.

distance.explanation: Ninety-one miles is a standard long gran fondo distance: enough to make fueling and durability decisive without crossing into an ultra.

climbing.explanation: The course gains 9,116 feet, and the three scored segments alone contain almost 4,800 feet of climbing.

descent_technicality.explanation: Remote Sonoma ribbon roads combine steep grades, narrow lanes, imperfect sight lines, and open traffic rather than closed-course alpine predictability.

road_surface.explanation: Although 96 percent paved, the route uses rough rural roads and a dirt section on Kruse Ranch Road; this is not fresh tarmac.

climate_risk.explanation: Coastal fog, ridge wind, and rapid temperature shifts can change grip and pacing even when March weather is broadly rideable.

altitude.explanation: The coastal mountains create steep relief without meaningful high-altitude exposure.

logistics.explanation: Monte Rio is a small regional base roughly two hours from major Bay Area airports, with adequate but limited lodging and no camping at the venue.

prestige.explanation: King Ridge has roughly two decades of Grasshopper history and recurring national cycling coverage, but is not a mass international gran fondo.

organization.explanation: Chip-timed segments, aid stations, medical and mechanical support are solid, but the event operates on open roads without full closures.

scenic_experience.explanation: Redwoods, coastal mountains, remote ridges, and a route local clubs call a crown-jewel North Bay ride create a consistently memorable day.

community_culture.explanation: Neutral riding between segments, a full lunch, a weekend shakeout and social ride, and deep Grasshopper roots make the social structure part of the event rather than decoration.

field_depth.explanation: The 2026 results included Brennan Wertz, Flavia Oliveira, Jen Tavé, and Peter Stetina, reflecting a strong national-level mixed-discipline field.

value.explanation: Timing, two aid stations, medical and mechanical support, event photos, lunch, and a full weekend program provide strong inclusions, although the current page omits price.

expenses.explanation: For Bay Area and Northern California riders this is generally a $300-500 regional weekend rather than a flight-based destination event.

cultural_impact.explanation: The route is a North Bay road-cycling landmark and the event receives national media attention, while remaining smaller than an iconic international fondo.

climb_profile.king_of_mountain: Cumulative time across three official segments

course_description.character: A 96-percent paved Sonoma County loop where the social neutral miles and three all-out climbing segments demand two different kinds of discipline.
course_description.signature_challenge: The three timed segments total roughly 23 miles and nearly 4,800 feet of climbing, so riders must recover on open roads without letting the whole 91-mile day become one uncontrolled effort.

suffering_zones.label: Joy Road
suffering_zones.description: The 10.8-mile opening timed segment gains 1,747 feet and establishes the ranking before the day is half over.

suffering_zones.label: Meyers Grade
suffering_zones.description: A shorter 4.9-mile segment gains 1,291 feet and rewards high sustainable climbing power.

suffering_zones.label: Kruse Road
suffering_zones.description: The final seven-mile scored climb adds 1,743 feet after 60 miles of riding.

logistics.airport: San Francisco, Oakland, or Sonoma County airports
logistics.lodging_strategy: Book Monte Rio, Guerneville, or nearby Sonoma lodging early; no camping was available at the 2026 venue.
logistics.transport: A car is the practical option. Riders roll from the Monte Rio Community Center to the first timed segment on open public roads.
logistics.food: The 2026 event included two aid stations and a post-ride lunch.

history.origin_story: Grasshopper has used Sonoma County roads for decades; King Ridge has been a named series fixture for roughly twenty years.
notable_moments: Brennan Wertz and Jen Tavé won the 2025 edition.
Gavin Sherry and Flavia Oliveira won the 2026 cumulative timed-segment competition.
history.reputation: A hard, scenic North Bay road classic with a mixed gravel-series audience.

biased_opinion.verdict: A road race with gravel manners
biased_opinion.summary: King Ridge does not belong in Gravel God simply because Grasshopper promotes it. The official facts say 96 percent pavement, road-bike setup, and timed road climbs; Roadie Labs is the honest home.
strengths: Social neutral sections between hard timed efforts
weaknesses: Current organizer page does not preserve price or a 2027 date
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A Tier 2 target for riders who want fondo distance, race-grade climbing, and a less transactional community format.

final_verdict.one_liner: A Sonoma road classic where 4 percent dirt matters less than 9,116 feet of climbing.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes when the organizer publishes the next edition. Train it as a road-climbing fondo with repeated threshold efforts, not as a gravel race.
final_verdict.alternatives: Levi's GranFondo for a larger production; Grasshopper Low Gap for a dirt-primary NorCal race.
